_comment: Registration for scripts/project-next-ownership.py (issue #1069).
REPLACES controls/project-next-vendor, which is retired with the gate it
scored. Those cases are NOT edited into this shape: they encode the
upstream-fidelity question ('does our copy match what codex-power-pack
published'), and this gate asks a different one. Editing a case to fit a
new question keeps the file and loses the distinction it drew.
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): it is a gate that lets
work THROUGH - a prerequisite of `make verify`, whose green is read as
'the engine CPP ships is the one CPP pinned' by sessions that do not
re-derive it. Nothing downstream re-derives it, and after #1069 there is
no upstream comparison left to catch a drifted file by accident.
WHAT THE GATE IS FOR, which decides the known-bad case: contract_version
is consumer-facing - it pins .project-next.json through the schema, it is
the runtime pin /project:next reads, and it is rendered into every report.
A silent edit to lib/project_next that leaves that version alone is the
change that breaks a consumer while every check stays green.
THE CASES CARRY ALL 11 PINNED PATHS, and must: the manifest key set is
checked against the hardcoded contract BEFORE any hash is compared, so a
case with fewer paths is refused for the wrong reason and never reaches
the comparison under test. The contract document additionally has to carry
a derivable 'Contract version `1.3`' line, or the good case fails on the
version path rather than passing on the hash path.
Stdlib-only, network-free and git-free, like the gate.
detect_signal: ^DRIFT: .* does not match the manifest pin\.$
limits: Covers the OFFLINE per-file hash comparison. It says nothing about whether the REAL engine tree is correct - that is the gate's own run under `make verify`, over the real tree. The derived-contract-version path, the unpinned-module scan and the dropped-pin refusal each need a differently-malformed input and a case can only carry one, so they are exercised by tests/test_project_next_ownership.py instead.

cases.name: bad-drifted-file
cases.why: One line appended to lib/project_next/rank.py with its pin untouched - an edit to the engine that never re-pinned. Per-file pins exist so a failure names the exact file; if this scores GOOD they name nothing, and after #1069 no upstream comparison remains to catch it instead.

cases.name: good-pinned-files
cases.why: The same 11-file tree with every file matching its pin and the document's contract version agreeing with the manifest. Separates a working gate from one wedged at 'fail', which the bad case alone cannot do - and this gate is a prerequisite of `make verify`, so a wedged one blocks every merge.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, not historical: the ownership gate is new at #1069, so no earlier version of it exists to anchor on and inventing one would be a fiction. This is the plausible weaker check written instead: confirm every pinned path is present and call that owned - 'complete' mistaken for 'correct'. It catches a deleted file and is blind to one edited in place. It MISSES the known-bad input and AGREES with the current gate on the known-good one.
